mainTopic: Half-כזית pieces of נבלה on a hide or a wood chip: when touching or carrying them makes a person טמא
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier discussion: רבי יוחנן's statement is about a thin layer of flesh (מרודד) stuck to a נבלה hide. Next the גמרא turns to the משנה's case of two half-כזית pieces on a hide, where רבי ישמעאל says the hide makes a person טמא by carrying but not by touching. בר פדא says this applies only to touching the outside, because touching the two pieces one after the other from the inside adds up. רבי יוחנן says separate touches never add up, and he links רבי ישמעאל to רבי דוסא בן הרכינס, who says separate coverings of an אהל do not add up. רב עוקבא בר חמא challenges בר פדא from a ברייתא, and רבא answers that רבי עקיבא requires touching to be possible from every side. Then רב אויא סבא asks whether, for רבי ישמעאל, a sealed thigh bone makes impure by carrying, and רבה בר רב הונא dodges the question because he is tired. עולא rules that two half-pieces stuck on a wood chip do not make impure by carrying, because the כזית must be carried all at once by itself. The גמרא defends him with the thin-layer answer and shows that רבי אליעזר in a ברייתא holds his view. Finally, a new משנה begins about the thigh bone of a human corpse.

steps.title: The flesh in question is a thin layer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes the earlier discussion. Both the earlier case and this case are about a thin layer of flesh (מרודד) attached to the hide.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is talking about a thin layer. Here too, it is talking about a thin layer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the previous discussion. Its answer is that the flesh being discussed is a thin, spread-out layer stuck to the hide, in the earlier case and in this one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A thin smear of flesh attached to a hide is not treated as a real piece of meat on its own. It counts as part of the hide and loses its own identity, even if it adds up to a כזית or more. Reading רבי יוחנן's statement as being about such a layer removes the difficulty raised before this point.

keyTerms.meaning: Spread thin, flattened; a thin layer of flesh stuck to the hide
Here too; the same answer applies to this case

steps.whatToRemember: A thin layer of flesh stuck to a hide is treated as part of the hide, not as a separate piece of meat.

phrases.english: It refers to a thin layer,
phrases.notes: This finishes a discussion that began before this line. A thin layer of flesh is stuck to the hide.

phrases.english: here too, it refers to a thin layer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a discussion that started before this section
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining the case narrowly (אוקימתא): the flesh is a thin layer
steps.terutzMaskana: Both statements are about a thin layer of flesh, which counts as part of the hide

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: two half-olive pieces on the hide
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה, the case where two half-olive pieces of flesh were on the hide.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: "If there were on it…"
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting a new topic by quoting the opening words of a line in the משנה. This is a setup line that gets us ready for בר פדא's comment in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full משנה line says: if two half-olive pieces of נבלה flesh were on a hide, the hide makes things טמא through carrying but not through touching. That is the view of רבי ישמעאל. The next steps ask exactly how far the 'no touching' rule goes.

keyTerms.meaning: "There were on it"; the opening words of the משנה line about two half-olive pieces on the hide
The opening words of a source, quoted to show which line is being discussed

phrases.english: "If there were upon it…"
phrases.notes: These are the first words of the משנה's case: two half-olive pieces of flesh sitting on the hide.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the thin-layer discussion to a new line of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two half-olive pieces on a hide: the hide makes things טמא through carrying, not through touching (רבי ישמעאל)

steps.title: בר פדא: the rule applies only to touching from outside
steps.stepSummary: בר פדא says the 'no טומאה by touching' ruling applies only to touching the outside of the hide. If you touch the pieces of flesh themselves on the inside, the two touches add up.
steps.simpleTranslation: בר פדא said: This was taught only about touching from the outside of the hide. But from the inside, there is such a thing as touching and then touching again.
steps.whatsHappening: בר פדא limits רבי ישמעאל's ruling. Touching the outer side of the hide does not make a person טמא, but touching the two half-pieces directly from the inside does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Touching the outside of the hide means you never touch the flesh at all, so there is no טומאה. If you touch one half-olive piece and then touch the other half-olive piece, בר פדא holds the two touches join together into a full כזית of contact. That makes you טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this about…; a phrase that narrows a ruling
From behind it; touching the outer side of the hide
From in front of it; touching the flesh side directly
Touches and then touches again; the idea that two separate touches of less than a כזית add up

steps.confusionAlert: בר פדא is not arguing with רבי ישמעאל. He accepts that touching does not make you טמא, but he says this holds only when you touch from the outside of the hide.

phrases.english: Bar Padda said:
They taught this only from behind it,
phrases.notes: "Behind it" means touching the outer side of the hide, so you never touch the flesh.

phrases.english: but from in front of it,
there is such a thing as touching and touching again.
phrases.notes: He means touching one half-piece and then the other, and the two touches combine into a full olive's worth.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר בַּר פְּדָא: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא מֵאַחֲרָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains and limits the משנה line quoted in step 2
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Touching from the inside makes a person טמא, because separate touches combine (יש נוגע וחוזר ונוגע)

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: separate touches never add up
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן disagrees with בר פדא. Touching once and then touching again does not combine into one full measure.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: There is no such thing as touching and touching again.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן argues with בר פדא and rejects the idea that two separate touches combine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן, each touch is judged on its own. Each touch here is of only half a כזית, so none of them reaches the amount needed for טומאה. That means even touching from the inside does not make a person טמא in רבי ישמעאל's case.

keyTerms.meaning: There is no combining of separate touches; each touch is judged alone

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
There is no touching and touching again,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: אֵין נוֹגֵעַ וְחוֹזֵר וְנוֹגֵעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with בר פדא's statement in step 3
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Separate touches of less than a כזית do not combine

steps.title: רבי יוחנן is consistent with his other teaching
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that רבי יוחנן's view fits another statement of his: that רבי ישמעאל and רבי דוסא בן הרכינס held the same principle.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן follows his own reasoning, because רבי יוחנן said: רבי ישמעאל and רבי דוסא בן הרכינס said the same thing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that רבי יוחנן is not saying something new here. It fits a statement he made elsewhere, linking רבי ישמעאל with רבי דוסא בן הרכינס. This sets up the explanation of that link, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "אזדא לטעמיה" means a sage's view in one place matches his view in another place. רבי יוחנן said that two תנאים held "one thing," meaning one shared principle. The גמרא is about to show that this shared principle is the same one behind his ruling here.

keyTerms.meaning: He goes according to his own reasoning; he is consistent with his view elsewhere
One thing; the same principle

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan follows his own reasoning,
as Rabbi Yoḥanan said:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל וְרַבִּי דּוֹסָא בֶּן הַרְכִּינָס
phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael and Rabbi Dosa ben Harkinas
said one thing.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַזְדָּא רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לְטַעְמֵיהּ, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that רבי יוחנן's view in step 4 matches another teaching of his
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's position that separate touches do not combine
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's own statement that רבי ישמעאל and רבי דוסא בן הרכינס held the same principle

steps.title: Naming the sources for רבי ישמעאל and רבי דוסא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא identifies where each of the two תנאים states the shared principle: רבי ישמעאל in our משנה, and רבי דוסא בן הרכינס in a משנה about טומאת אהל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל's view is what we already said. רבי דוסא בן הרכינס's view is from a משנה: if something that makes impure through an אהל was split into two pieces and both were brought into a house, רבי דוסא says the house stays pure, and the חכמים say it becomes impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is filling in the details of רבי יוחנן's statement by pointing to where each sage said his ruling. This sets up the comparison in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל's source is our own משנה, where touching the two half-pieces on the hide does not make a person impure. רבי דוסא's source is a case of a dead body's piece split in two under one roof, where he says the two halves do not add up to the full measure.

keyTerms.meaning: Things, like parts of a dead body, that make everything under the same roof impure
That were split into pieces
Rules it pure
The Sages, the majority opinion

phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael — that which we said;
Rabbi Dosa ben Harkinas — as we learned in a Mishnah:
All things that make impure through a tent,
that were divided, and one brought them into the house —
phrases.notes: Each piece alone is less than the full measure, but together they make a full measure.

phrases.english: Rabbi Dosa ben Harkinas declares it pure,
and the Sages declare it impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל – הָא דַּאֲמַרַן; רַבִּי דּוֹסָא בֶּן הַרְכִּינָס – דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the actual sources behind רבי יוחנן's claim in step 5.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's claim that רבי ישמעאל and רבי דוסא hold the same principle
steps.raayaSupportSource: Our משנה for רבי ישמעאל, and the משנה in אהלות for רבי דוסא בן הרכינס

steps.title: Covering twice is like touching twice
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows the shared principle: רבי דוסא says covering twice does not combine, and רבי ישמעאל says touching twice does not combine.
steps.simpleTranslation: Didn't רבי דוסא בן הרכינס say there that covering one piece and then covering another does not add up? Here too, touching one piece and then touching another does not add up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא connects the two rulings and shows they come from the same idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי דוסא's case the roof covers each half-piece separately, so the two coverings do not combine. That matches רבי ישמעאל, who says two separate touches do not combine. This completes the proof for רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: Covering or overshadowing something, forming an אהל over it
And then again
Touching

steps.whatToRemember: The shared principle is that two separate contacts with half-measures, whether touching or covering, do not combine into one full measure.

phrases.aramaic: לָאו אָמַר רַבִּי דּוֹסָא בֶּן הַרְכִּינָס הָתָם,
phrases.english: Didn't Rabbi Dosa ben Harkinas say there,
there is no "covering and then covering again",

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא נָמֵי אֵין נוֹגֵעַ וְחוֹזֵר וְנוֹגֵעַ.
phrases.english: here too there is no "touching and then touching again."

steps.triggerLanguage: לָאו אָמַר רַבִּי דּוֹסָא בֶּן הַרְכִּינָס הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the source cited in step 6 matches רבי ישמעאל.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי דוסא and רבי ישמעאל share one principle
steps.raayaSupportSource: The parallel between אין מאהיל וחוזר ומאהיל and אין נוגע וחוזר ונוגע

steps.title: The strict חכמים cannot match the lenient רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: If רבי דוסא matches רבי ישמעאל, then the חכמים who argue with רבי דוסא should match רבי עקיבא. But the חכמים are strict and רבי עקיבא is lenient.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since רבי דוסא בן הרכינס matches רבי ישמעאל, do the חכמים match רבי עקיבא? But רבי עקיבא rules pure!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's pairing by pointing out that the opponents on each side do not line up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In our משנה, רבי עקיבא is more lenient than רבי ישמעאל: he says pure for both touching and carrying. The חכמים are more strict than רבי דוסא: they say impure. So the pairs seem backwards.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis, here the חכמים who argue with רבי דוסא
He actually rules pure

phrases.aramaic: וּמִדְּרַבִּי דּוֹסָא בֶּן הַרְכִּינָס כְּרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל,
phrases.english: And since Rabbi Dosa ben Harkinas is like Rabbi Yishmael,
are the Rabbis like Rabbi Akiva?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא טַהוֹרֵי קָא מְטַהַר!
phrases.english: But Rabbi Akiva declares pure!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִדְּרַבִּי דּוֹסָא בֶּן הַרְכִּינָס כְּרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל, רַבָּנַן כְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the pairing that steps 5–7 just established.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's pairing of רבי ישמעאל with רבי דוסא בן הרכינס
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If one side lines up, the opponents should line up too. But רבי עקיבא is more lenient while the חכמים are more strict.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא is lenient only because of the hide
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא rules pure only when the pieces are on a hide. In general he holds the half-pieces combine and make impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא rules pure only with the hide. But in general he rules impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי עקיבא's leniency is special to the hide case, so in general he is strict like the חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The leniency does not come from a view that two half-pieces never combine. It comes from something about the hide itself. So on the basic question of combining, רבי עקיבא matches the strict חכמים after all.

keyTerms.meaning: Only in this case does he say so, and not elsewhere
In general, in ordinary cases

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָא מְטַהַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva only declares pure
with the hide,
but in general he declares impure,

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד כָּאן לָא קָא מְטַהַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אֶלָּא בְּעוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of a ruling: the leniency belongs only to a special case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי עקיבא holds that half-pieces never combine, so he cannot match the strict חכמים.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי עקיבא holds that half-pieces do combine. He is lenient only because of the hide, so he matches the חכמים.

steps.title: Proof from the end of the משנה: the hide cancels the pieces
steps.stepSummary: The end of the משנה says רבי עקיבא agrees that two half-pieces stuck on a wood chip and moved make a person impure. He rules pure with the hide only because the hide cancels them.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the end of the משנה teaches: רבי עקיבא agrees that if someone stuck two half-olive pieces on a wood chip and moved them, he is impure. Why does רבי עקיבא rule pure with the hide? Because the hide cancels them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings proof for its answer from the end of our own משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a wood chip, רבי עקיבא agrees the two halves combine and make the carrier impure. So his pure ruling with the hide must come from the hide itself, which cancels the pieces. This confirms that in general he is strict like the חכמים.

keyTerms.meaning: The end part of the משנה
Agrees
A wood chip or splinter
Moved them, which counts as carrying for טומאה
Cancels them, makes them lose their importance

steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא's leniency is about the hide, not about combining. So the pairing stands: רבי ישמעאל matches רבי דוסא, and רבי עקיבא matches the חכמים.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't conclude that רבי עקיבא thinks half-pieces never combine. He does think they combine. The hide is what makes the difference.

phrases.english: as the end of the Mishnah teaches:

phrases.aramaic: וּמוֹדֶה רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא בִּשְׁנֵי חֲצָאֵי זֵיתִים
phrases.english: And Rabbi Akiva agrees regarding two half-olive pieces
that one stuck on a wood chip and moved them, that he is impure.

phrases.aramaic: וּמִפְּנֵי מָה רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא מְטַהֵר בָּעוֹר?
phrases.english: And why does Rabbi Akiva declare pure with the hide?
Because the hide cancels them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 9 with a source.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי עקיבא in general holds half-pieces combine, and is lenient only because of the hide
steps.raayaSupportSource: The end of our משנה: ומודה רבי עקיבא בשני חצאי זיתים שתחבן בקיסם

steps.title: A ברייתא about a hide with two half-pieces of carcass
steps.stepSummary: רב עוקבא בר חמא quotes a ברייתא. רבי ישמעאל says the hide with two half-pieces makes impure by carrying. רבי עקיבא says that whatever cannot make impure by touching cannot make impure by carrying.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב עוקבא בר חמא objected from a ברייתא: "Their carcass" teaches that a hide with two half olive-bulks on it does not make impure. Might it not make impure even by carrying? The verse says "and whoever carries shall be impure". This is רבי ישמעאל's view. רבי עקיבא says: "Whoever touches" and "whoever carries" are linked. What can make impure by touching can make impure by carrying. What cannot make impure by touching cannot make impure by carrying.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that will be used for an objection in the next step. Right now it is only quoting the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both תנאים agree that touching the hide does not make a person impure. They argue about carrying. רבי ישמעאל learns from a separate phrase that carrying makes impure. רבי עקיבא links carrying to touching: no touching means no carrying.

keyTerms.meaning: The carcass of an animal that died without proper שחיטה
Becoming impure by touching
Becoming impure by carrying or moving
Enters the category of

phrases.english: Rav Ukva bar Chama raises an objection:
"Their carcass" – but not a hide
that has on it two half olive-bulks.
Might one think it does not make impure even by carrying?
The verse says: "And whoever carries shall be impure"
– these are the words of Rabbi Yishmael.
Rabbi Akiva says: "Whoever touches" and "whoever carries"
whatever enters the category of contact
enters the category of carrying;
whatever does not enter the category of contact
does not enter the category of carrying.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to object to בר פדא's claim in step 3 that, for רבי ישמעאל, separate touches from the inside combine.
steps.raayaObject: An objection to בר פדא's claim that touching the half-pieces from the inside combines
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading the words נבלתם, הנוגע and והנושא

steps.title: But the pieces can be touched from the inside
steps.stepSummary: If בר פדא is right that two separate touches combine from the inside, then the hide case does fall into the category of touching. So how can רבי עקיבא in the ברייתא say there is no touching here, and therefore no carrying?
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it is so, look, it does enter the category of contact from the inside!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the ברייתא to challenge בר פדא. If touching the pieces from the inside counts as touching, then רבי עקיבא's reason in the ברייתא would not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בר פדא said in step 3 that touching one half-piece and then the other from the inside adds up to a full touch. If so, the hide case does count as touching. Then רבי עקיבא's rule (no touching, so no carrying) should not exempt it, and the ברייתא seems to contradict בר פדא.

keyTerms.meaning: And if it is so
From the inside, the side of the hide where the flesh is

phrases.english: And if it is so,
phrases.notes: If בר פדא is right that two touches from the inside combine, as he said in step 3.

phrases.english: look, it does enter the category of contact from the inside!
phrases.notes: From the inside means the inner face of the hide, where the pieces of flesh sit uncovered.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם אִיתָא הֲרֵי בָּא לִכְלַל מַגָּע מִלְּפָנָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא from step 11 to attack בר פדא's claim from step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: בר פדא's claim (step 3) that separate touches from the inside combine (יש נוגע וחוזר ונוגע)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If touches from the inside combine, the hide case does count as contact, so רבי עקיבא's rule 'no contact, no carrying' would not exempt it. The ברייתא therefore seems to show that inside contact does not count, against בר פדא.

steps.title: רבא: contact must be possible from every side
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that רבי עקיבא means contact from every side. Since touching the outside of the hide does not make impure, carrying does not make impure either.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: This is what he means. Whatever can make impure by touching from every side can make impure by carrying. Whatever cannot make impure by touching from every side cannot make impure by carrying.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question by explaining what רבי עקיבא really meant by contact.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Touching from the inside is not enough. To make impure by carrying, the item must make impure by touching from every side, including the outside of the hide. Here touching the outside does nothing, so carrying does nothing either.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he means (explaining a statement)
From every side

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, רבי עקיבא's rule means that only something which makes impure by touching from every side makes impure by carrying. The hide with two half-pieces fails this test, so it is pure even when carried.

phrases.english: Rava said: This is what he means:

phrases.aramaic: אֶת שֶׁבָּא לִכְלַל מַגָּע בְּכׇל צַד –
phrases.english: whatever enters the category of contact from every side
enters the category of carrying;

phrases.aramaic: לֹא בָּא לִכְלַל מַגָּע בְּכׇל צַד –
phrases.english: whatever does not enter the category of contact from every side
does not enter the category of carrying.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 12 by reading רבי עקיבא's words more precisely, so בר פדא's claim stands.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of the ברייתא more precisely
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Contact from any one side, such as from the inside, would be enough for רבי עקיבא's rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: Contact must be possible from every side, including the outside of the hide. Since it is not, carrying does not make impure.

steps.title: A new question: the sealed thigh bone according to רבי ישמעאל
steps.stepSummary: רב אויא סבא asks רבה בר רב הונא whether a קולית סתומה makes a person impure by carrying, according to רבי ישמעאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אויא סבא asked רבה בר רב הונא: A sealed thigh bone, according to רבי ישמעאל, what is the law? Does it make impure?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question is asked about a sealed bone that has marrow inside. The question is whether רבי ישמעאל would say it makes a person impure when he carries it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A sealed bone cannot make impure by touching, because nobody can reach the marrow inside. In the hide case, רבי ישמעאל ruled that carrying makes impure even though touching the outside does not. So we want to know if he says the same about this bone.

keyTerms.meaning: A sealed thigh bone. The marrow is inside and cannot be reached.
What is the law? This is the standard way to open a question.
That it makes impure. Here it means impurity by carrying.

steps.confusionAlert: Nobody is asking whether the sealed bone makes impure by touching. Everyone agrees it does not. The question is only about carrying it.

phrases.english: Rav Avya the Elder asked
of Rabba bar Rav Huna:
A sealed thigh bone, according to Rabbi Yishmael,
phrases.notes: This is a bone with marrow inside that is closed up, so you cannot touch the marrow. The משנה discusses it later.

phrases.english: what is the law, does it make impure?
phrases.notes: He means impure through carrying it.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַב אַוְיָא סָבָא מֵרַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining רבי עקיבא's view, the גמרא turns to רבי ישמעאל and asks how his view applies to a new case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a sealed bone, which cannot be touched at all, make impure by carrying according to רבי ישמעאל?

steps.title: The two possible ways to understand רבי ישמעאל
steps.stepSummary: Option one: רבי ישמעאל agrees that only what can be touched makes impure by carrying. In the hide case, the flesh can be touched from inside. Option two: he does not hold that rule at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי ישמעאל hold the rule that whatever can make impure by touching can make impure by carrying, and whatever cannot make impure by touching cannot make impure by carrying? If so, his reason in the hide case is that the flesh can be touched from the inside. Or perhaps he does not hold this rule?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the question is hard by giving two ways to understand רבי ישמעאל. Each way leads to a different answer about the sealed bone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי ישמעאל holds the rule, he ruled impure in the hide case only because the flesh can be touched from inside. Then the sealed bone, which cannot be touched at all, would be pure. If he does not hold the rule, carrying makes impure even without any touching, so the sealed bone would make impure.

keyTerms.meaning: Comes into the category of touching. It can make impure by touching.
Carrying. A person can become impure by carrying something impure.
From the inside. Here it means touching the flesh directly on the inside of the hide.
Or perhaps. This brings in the second side of a question.
He holds this view / he does not hold this view.

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the same rule that רבי עקיבא used in step 11. The question is whether רבי ישמעאל also agrees to it, and only disagrees about how it applies to the hide.

phrases.english: Does Rabbi Yishmael hold:
whatever comes into the category of touching
comes into the category of carrying,
whatever does not come into the category of touching
does not come into the category of carrying,
and here, this is the reason
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the hide case from the ברייתא in step 11, where רבי ישמעאל ruled impure.

phrases.english: because it comes into the category of touching from the inside.
Or perhaps he does not hold this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It lays out the two sides of the question asked in step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does רבי ישמעאל accept the rule that carrying depends on the possibility of touching, or does he not?

steps.title: The question is dodged with 'a raven is flying'
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב הונא does not answer. He distracts רב אויא by saying 'a raven is flying,' so the question is left open.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: A raven is flying.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר רב הונא does not give a real answer. He points to a raven in the sky to change the subject.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not choose either side of the question. So we are not told whether רבי ישמעאל holds the rule, and we are not told what the law is for the sealed bone.

keyTerms.meaning: A raven is flying. He says this to change the subject and avoid answering.

steps.whatToRemember: We do not know whether, according to רבי ישמעאל, a sealed bone makes impure by carrying. It depends on whether he holds the rule 'no touching, no carrying,' and the גמרא leaves that open.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not look for a hidden halachic meaning in 'a raven is flying.' He means it plainly as a distraction, and the question stays unanswered.

phrases.english: He said to him: A raven is flying.
phrases.notes: He is changing the subject so he does not have to answer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It is the response to the question in steps 14 and 15, but it is an evasion and not a real answer.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No real answer is given. He changes the subject, so the question stays unresolved.

steps.title: רבא asks why his father brushed off a great scholar
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks his father רבה בר רב הונא why he avoided רב אויא סבא, whom he himself used to praise as a great man.
steps.simpleTranslation: His son רבא said to him: Isn't this רב אויא סבא from פומבדיתא, the one you used to praise to us as a great man?
steps.whatsHappening: The story from the last step continues. רבא is surprised that his father dodged the question of a man he used to call a great scholar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 16, רבה בר רב הונא distracted רב אויא instead of answering. רבא points out the problem: you yourself told us he is a great man, so why treat his question that way? This sets up the father's explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: The Elder; a title added to רב אויא's name
פומבדיתא, a major Torah center in Babylonia
A great man, meaning a great Torah scholar

phrases.english: Rava, his son, said to him:

phrases.aramaic: וְלָאו הַיְינוּ רַב אַוְיָא סָבָא מִפּוּמְבְּדִיתָא,
phrases.english: But isn't this Rav Avya the Elder from Pumbedita,
whom the Master used to praise to us,
saying that he is a great man?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָאו הַיְינוּ רַב אַוְיָא סָבָא מִפּוּמְבְּדִיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the way the father avoided answering in step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבה בר רב הונא avoided answering someone he considered a great scholar.

steps.title: The father explains he was too tired for a hard question
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב הונא answers that he was worn out that day, and the question needed careful thinking.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Today I am in a state of 'support me with props' (I am tired), and he asked me something that needs real reasoning.
steps.whatsHappening: The father explains himself. He was too tired that day, and the question needed careful thought, so he could not answer right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He uses a פסוק from שיר השירים to say he was weak and needed support. He was not disrespecting רב אויא; the question was serious and he did not want to answer it carelessly. The question about קולית סתומה stays unanswered.

keyTerms.meaning: Support me with props; a פסוק used here to mean 'I am weak and tired'
A matter that needs reasoning and careful thought

steps.whatToRemember: The question from step 14 about קולית סתומה according to רבי ישמעאל was never answered. It was left open because it needed careful thinking.

phrases.english: He said to him:
Today I am "Support me with props,"
phrases.notes: שיר השירים 2:5. He means: I'm worn out today and need something to lean on.

phrases.english: and he asked me a matter
that requires reasoning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's question from step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He was tired, and the question needed careful thought, so he did not answer it on the spot.

steps.title: Two half-olive pieces on a wood chip do not make impure by carrying
steps.stepSummary: עולא rules that if two half-כזית pieces of נבלה are stuck on a wood chip, a person carrying them stays pure, even if he carries them around all day.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: Two half-olive pieces that someone skewered on a wood chip, even if he carries them back and forth all day long, he stays pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new teaching. עולא says two half-pieces joined only by a stick do not make a person impure by carrying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally you need a full כזית of נבלה to become impure by משא. Here the two halves together make a כזית, but they are held together only by a stick. עולא says that does not count, and the next step gives his reason.

keyTerms.meaning: Half olive-sized pieces; two halves together equal one כזית
A wood chip or small stick
Moves back and forth, carries around
Pure, not impure

phrases.english: Ulla said:
Two half olive-bulks
that one skewered on a wood chip,
even if he moves them back and forth
the entire day, he is pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about joining half-pieces for impurity by carrying.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two half-כזית pieces joined only by a wood chip do not make a person impure by משא.

steps.title: The source: the כזית must be carried all at once by itself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains עולא's reason from the פסוק: it is written 'is carried' but read 'carries', so the כזית must be able to be carried all at once on its own.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? It is written 'וְנִשָּׂא' (is carried) but we read it 'נוֹשֵׂא' (carries). We need a person who carries, and also that the piece is carried all at once.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source for עולא's rule. It uses the difference between how the word is written and how it is read in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The read form 'נוֹשֵׂא' teaches that a person who carries becomes impure. The written form 'נִשָּׂא' adds that the meat itself must be 'carried', meaning it can be lifted as one piece all at once. Two halves on a stick are only carried together because of the stick, so they do not qualify.

keyTerms.meaning: It is written; how the word is spelled in the תורה
We read; how the word is traditionally pronounced
Carries; the person doing the carrying
Is carried; the object being carried
All at once, as one unit

steps.confusionAlert: Both halves together do equal a כזית. The problem is not the size; it is that they are not carried as one piece by themselves, only through the stick.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
It is written "and is carried"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 11:40. The letters can be read as 'is carried', even though we pronounce it 'carries'.

phrases.english: and we read "carries";
we require "carries"
and that it be carried all at once.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא כְּתִיב וְנִשָּׂא וְקָרֵינַן נוֹשֵׂא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the scriptural reason for עולא's ruling in step 19.
steps.raayaObject: עולא's rule that half-pieces on a wood chip do not make impure by carrying.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The written vs. read form of the word in ויקרא 11:40: 'נשא' written as 'is carried', read as 'carries'.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule, that the כזית must be carried all at once, is exactly what the next step uses to challenge עולא.

steps.title: Challenge from רבי ישמעאל: half-pieces on a hide do make impure by carrying
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges עולא from the משנה, where רבי ישמעאל says two half-pieces on a hide make impure by carrying, even though they are not carried as one piece by themselves.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: If there were two half-olive pieces on the hide, they make impure by carrying but not by touching; these are the words of רבי ישמעאל. Why? This is not 'carried all at once'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks עולא's rule using the משנה. In the משנה, two half-pieces on a hide make a person impure by carrying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to עולא, half-pieces only count if they are carried as one unit by themselves. On the hide, the two halves are only carried together because of the hide, just like the wood chip. So why does רבי ישמעאל say they make impure by carrying?

keyTerms.meaning: Make impure by carrying
But not by touching
Why? A word that opens a challenge

phrases.aramaic: תְּנַן: הָיוּ עָלָיו שְׁנֵי חֲצָאֵי זֵיתִים –
phrases.english: We learned: If there were on it two half olive-bulks,
they make impure by carrying but not by touching;
these are the words of Rabbi Yishmael.
Why? But it is not carried all at once!

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן הָיוּ עָלָיו שְׁנֵי חֲצָאֵי זֵיתִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges עולא's rule and its source from steps 19-20.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's rule that half-pieces joined by something else do not make impure by carrying.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the משנה, רבי ישמעאל says two half-pieces on a hide make impure by carrying, even though they are joined only through the hide and not carried as one unit by themselves.

steps.title: The pieces were joined by a thin strip of meat
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers the challenge from רבי ישמעאל. The two half-pieces on the hide were connected by a thin, flat layer of meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: The case is where there is a thin strip of meat joining them.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the challenge from רבי ישמעאל in the previous step. He says the two half-pieces in the משנה were linked by a thin layer of meat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the halves are joined by a strip of meat, they can be lifted together without the hide's help. So they really are 'carried as one piece by themselves,' just as עולא requires. That is why רבי ישמעאל can say they make טמא by carrying, and עולא's rule still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: A thin, flattened layer of meat that connects the two pieces
An olive's volume, the minimum amount of נבלה that makes a person טמא

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
[It is speaking] about a thin strip [of meat].
phrases.notes: He means a thin layer of meat on the hide links the two halves, so they can be lifted together without the hide.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא from רבי ישמעאל in step 21
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case in the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two halves were held together only by the hide, so they were not carryable by themselves
steps.terutzMaskana: A thin strip of meat joins them, so they can be carried together on their own, which fits עולא

steps.title: A challenge from רבי עקיבא's concession about a wood chip
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings another challenge to עולא. רבי עקיבא admits that two half-pieces stuck on a wood chip make a person טמא when moved, even though they cannot be carried as one by themselves.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי עקיבא agrees that if someone stuck two half-olive pieces on a wood chip and moved them, he is טמא. Why? They are not able to be carried on their own!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges עולא again, this time from רבי עקיבא's concession in the משנה. It is almost exactly עולא's own case, two halves on a wood chip, yet רבי עקיבא says the person is טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא said that halves held together by a wood chip are not considered 'carried', so the person stays טהור. רבי עקיבא rules that in the very same setup the person becomes טמא. That seems to contradict עולא directly.

keyTerms.meaning: Agrees or admits, even though he usually holds the other way
A wood chip or splinter
Moving or shifting something, which can make a person טמא even without lifting it fully
Able to be carried by itself as one unit

phrases.english: Come and hear:
Rabbi Akiva agrees
in the case of two half-olive pieces
that someone stuck on a wood chip
and moved them, that he is impure.
Why?
But it is not able to be carried [by itself]!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 22 resolved the first challenge, a new challenge from the same משנה is raised
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי עקיבא rules that halves on a wood chip make a person טמא when moved, which is exactly the case where עולא said the person stays טהור

steps.title: Here too, a thin strip joins the pieces
steps.stepSummary: The same answer works for רבי עקיבא. The halves were joined by a thin strip of meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, it is speaking about a thin strip of meat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with the same idea רב פפא used. In רבי עקיבא's case, a thin layer of meat also connects the two halves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a strip of meat joins the halves, the wood chip isn't what holds them together. They can be lifted as one by themselves, so the person becomes טמא even according to עולא.

keyTerms.meaning: Here too, the same answer applies

phrases.english: Here too, [it is speaking] about a thin strip [of meat].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 23 using רב פפא's answer from step 22
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case, same as step 22
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The wood chip alone held the halves together
steps.terutzMaskana: A thin strip of meat links them, so they are carryable by themselves
steps.whatToRemember: Both challenges to עולא are answered the same way. When the halves are joined by a thin strip of meat (מרודד), they count as one piece that can be carried on its own.

steps.title: עולא's idea appears in a dispute between תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that עולא's view is already the subject of a dispute in a ברייתא. The ברייתא lists 'one who touches' and 'one who moves', and רבי אליעזר adds 'even one who carries'.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like a dispute between תנאים: Both one who touches and one who moves [are טמא]. רבי אליעזר says: Even one who carries.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to show that עולא's idea is like one side of an older argument. This step sets up the next move, where the wording of the ברייתא will be questioned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא talks about two pieces of meat, each less than a כזית. On the surface, רבי אליעזר just adds 'carrying' to the list, which seems strange. The גמרא will soon explain what he really means.

keyTerms.meaning: Like a dispute between תנאים, the sages of the משנה era
One who touches
One who carries

phrases.english: This is like [a dispute between] תנאים:
Both one who touches and one who moves [are impure],
Rabbi Eliezer says:
Even one who carries.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending עולא, the גמרא now shows his view matches a tannaitic opinion
steps.raayaObject: That עולא's rule is held by one of the תנאים
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with the words of רבי אליעזר

steps.title: Isn't carrying already a kind of moving?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי אליעזר adds. Carrying always moves the object, so it should already be included in 'one who moves'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that to say that carrying is not moving?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the simple reading of רבי אליעזר's words. If the first part already covers someone who moves the meat, then someone who carries it is obviously included.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Anyone who carries something also moves it. So 'even one who carries' adds nothing if you read it simply. This pushes the גמרא to find a different meaning for רבי אליעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say? (a question showing an idea makes no sense)

phrases.english: Is that to say that one who carries is not one who moves?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the plain wording of the ברייתא quoted in step 25
steps.kashyaTarget: The plain reading of רבי אליעזר's words
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Carrying always includes moving, so adding 'one who carries' would add nothing

steps.title: רבי אליעזר requires that the meat be carryable by itself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the ברייתא. The first opinion says touching or moving makes טמא even when the meat cannot be carried by itself, and רבי אליעזר says it only makes טמא if it can.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't this what it is saying: Both one who touches and one who moves [are impure] even when it cannot be carried by itself. And רבי אליעזר comes to say: Only if it can be carried by itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the ברייתא is really an argument about whether the meat must be carryable on its own. רבי אליעזר's opinion is exactly עולא's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion does not care whether the pieces could be lifted together without help. רבי אליעזר adds a condition: the meat must be 'נישא', able to be carried as one by itself. So עולא is following רבי אליעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, isn't this what it means? (introduces a new reading of a text)
Only if, a condition that limits a rule

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows עולא is not inventing something new. His requirement that a כזית be carryable on its own is already the opinion of רבי אליעזר in a ברייתא.

phrases.english: Rather, isn't this what it is saying:
Both one who touches and one who moves [are impure]
even when it is not able to be carried [by itself],
and Rabbi Eliezer comes to say:
Only if it is able to be carried [by itself],

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 26 by rereading the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אליעזר is adding 'carrying' as another way to become טמא
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי אליעזר is adding a condition that the meat must be carryable by itself, like עולא

steps.title: But why does it say 'even'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the new reading. If רבי אליעזר is adding a limit, the word 'even' doesn't fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is 'even'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the word 'אף' (even) does not fit the new reading. 'Even' usually adds more cases, but רבי אליעזר is now limiting the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the new reading, רבי אליעזר makes the rule narrower, not wider. 'Even' sounds like he is adding cases, so the wording seems to work against the explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: Even, also (a word that usually adds to a rule)

phrases.english: And what is [the meaning of] 'even'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading offered in step 27
steps.kashyaTarget: The reinterpretation of רבי אליעזר in step 27
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word 'even' implies adding cases, but the new reading has רבי אליעזר limiting the rule

steps.title: Read it as 'only if it can be carried'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that we should read רבי אליעזר's words as 'only if it can be carried by itself', instead of 'even'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say: Only if it is able to be carried by itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the problem by changing how we read the words. Instead of 'even one who carries', read 'only if it can be carried by itself'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With this reading, the ברייתא clearly matches עולא. The first opinion makes a person טמא even without carryability, and רבי אליעזר requires it. So עולא follows רבי אליעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: Say, read it this way (the גמרא adjusts the wording)

steps.whatToRemember: עולא's rule, that a כזית must be carryable all at once by itself, is the opinion of רבי אליעזר in the ברייתא. The other תנא holds that touching or moving makes טמא even without that.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't read רבי אליעזר as adding a new way to become טמא. After the גמרא's reading he is limiting the rule: only meat that can be carried by itself makes a person טמא.

phrases.english: Say: Only if it is able to be carried [by itself].
phrases.notes: The גמרא is telling us to swap the word 'even' for 'only if', so the ברייתא fits.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 28
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adjusting the wording of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אליעזר's words say 'even one who carries'
steps.terutzMaskana: Read 'only if it can be carried by itself', so רבי אליעזר matches עולא
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: עולא's view follows רבי אליעזר in the ברייתא

steps.title: A new משנה opens with the thigh bone of a corpse
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה begins and names its subject: the thigh bone (קולית) of a human corpse (מת).
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: With regard to the thigh bone of a human corpse...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא's discussion is finished, and a new משנה begins. These first words only set up the topic; the ruling comes right after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing is being proven or challenged yet. The משנה is introducing the case it will discuss: a thigh bone that comes from a dead person. Keep this subject in mind, because the next words will tell us the הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה. Written short here as מַתְנִי׳, it marks the start of a new משנה
The thigh bone, the long bone of the leg
The dead person, a human corpse

steps.confusionAlert: Don't look for a ruling in these words yet. This is only the opening of the משנה, and the הלכה comes in the next words.

phrases.english: MISHNAH: The thigh bone of a corpse

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the discussion of עולא and רבי אליעזר's ברייתא ended in Step 29.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה introduces its case: a human corpse's thigh bone. The ruling follows in the continuation.
